title: Fuel duty
headline: 52.95p since 2022, with rises planned to 57.95p. Not raised since 2011.
description: Change fuel duty rates on petrol and diesel, as a percentage of the current rates.

baselinePolicy.text: Main rate 52.95p a litre. Budget 2025 cancelled the 2026-27 uprating and extended the 5p cut to 31 August 2026, then raises it by 1p from September 2026, 2p from December 2026 and 2p from March 2027 (Table 4.1 line 3).
alreadyIncludes: Fuel duty: 2026-27 uprating cancelled and the 5p cut phased out by March 2027 (Budget 2025, Table 4.1 line 3).

level.label: Fuel duty per litre
level.note: 52.95p today (since 23 March 2022). Budget 2025 planned rises of 1p in September 2026, 2p in December 2026 and 2p in March 2027, taking the rate to 57.95p before RPI uprating from April 2027; the level shown is your change applied to that planned rate.

uprating.head: fuelDuties
uprating.note: Shifted to the start year and scaled by the OBR March 2026 forecast for this receipts head (ADR-0004).

caveats: Sum of HMRC's petrol and diesel rows for a 1% change in duty; larger changes are scaled linearly.

HMRC's estimates are on its Spring Statement 2025 indexed baseline for an April 2026 start. This tool shifts the profile to the chosen start year and scales it by the growth of the relevant OBR receipts head in the March 2026 forecast; the underlying level is not rebased. HMRC deferred its 2026 edition to review key assumptions.

considerations.text: HMRC's figure is a direct effect on this tax and closely related tax bases. It includes HMRC's standard behavioural response (for personal taxes, through taxable income elasticities and tax-motivated incorporation), but not wider effects on the economy such as inflation or investment, which HMRC says are usually captured in the OBR's economy forecast instead.

HMRC postponed the 2026 edition of these estimates (due 7 July 2026) to complete a review of the key assumptions behind some of them, after the Office for Statistics Regulation asked for more transparency about pre- and post-behavioural estimates. The figures here are HMRC's June 2025 estimates.

interactions.text: Both change fuel duty rates: restoring the cancelled uprating and moving rates by a percentage overlap, so the combined effect is approximate.
